context.heading: A curated reference for modern language-model architectures
context.after: The gallery focuses on text-only LLMs and language-model backbones. For multimodal releases, cards usually describe the text decoder/backbone rather than every vision, audio, or image-generation component.

context.heading: GPT-2 XL (1.5B)
context.after: Late-2019 dense baseline included here as a reference point for how much decoder stacks have changed since GPT-2.

context.heading: Llama 3 (8B)
context.after: Reference dense Llama stack used to contrast OLMo 2's normalization and attention choices.

context.heading: Llama 3.2 (1B)
context.after: Small dense Llama baseline in the Qwen comparison, with fewer layers but more width.

context.heading: OLMo 2 (7B)
context.after: Transparent dense model that keeps classic MHA and pushes normalization changes for training stability.

context.heading: DeepSeek V3 (671B)
context.after: DeepSeek's flagship template kicked off the recent wave of large open MoE models.

context.heading: DeepSeek R1 (671B)
context.after: Reasoning-tuned DeepSeek model built on the V3 architecture rather than a new base design.

context.heading: Gemma 3 (27B)
context.after: Gemma's flagship text stack leans on local attention more aggressively than Gemma 2.

context.heading: Mistral Small 3.1 (24B)
context.after: Fast dense 24B model that drops the sliding-window setup used in older Mistral releases.

context.heading: Llama 4 Maverick (400B)
context.after: Meta's large MoE follows the DeepSeek V3 playbook but with a more conventional attention stack.

context.heading: Qwen3 (0.6B)
context.after: Tiny current-generation Qwen model that trades width for more depth and a low memory footprint.

context.heading: Qwen3 (235B-A22B)
context.after: Large sparse Qwen variant that stays very close to DeepSeek V3 while removing the shared expert.

context.heading: Qwen3 (30B-A3B)
context.after: Small sparse Qwen3 model that sits close to GPT-OSS in active size but uses a deeper stack.

context.heading: Qwen3 (32B)
context.after: Large dense Qwen3 model that serves as the clearest like-for-like comparison for OLMo 3 32B.

context.heading: Qwen3 (4B)
context.after: Mid-size dense Qwen3 model used here as a clean baseline against SmolLM3 and Tiny Aya.

context.heading: Qwen3 (8B)
context.after: Dense Qwen3 baseline used here to show how little OLMo 3 changed the overall decoder recipe.

context.heading: SmolLM3 (3B)
context.after: Compact dense model that experiments with leaving out positional encodings in selected layers.

context.heading: Kimi K2 (1T)
context.after: Trillion-parameter Moonshot model that essentially scales the DeepSeek V3 recipe upward.

context.heading: GLM-4.5 (355B)
context.after: Agent-oriented instruction/reasoning hybrid that borrows DeepSeek's dense-prefix MoE layout.

context.heading: GPT-OSS (120B)
context.after: Larger gpt-oss variant keeps the same alternating-attention recipe as the 20B model.

context.heading: GPT-OSS (20B)
context.after: OpenAI's smaller open-weight MoE model favors width and alternating local/global attention.

context.heading: Gemma 3 (270M)
context.after: Tiny Gemma 3 variant that preserves the family's local-global attention recipe at a toy scale.

context.heading: Grok 2.5 (270B)
context.after: Rare production-model release that shows an older MoE style with fewer, larger experts.

context.heading: Qwen3 Next (80B-A3B)
context.after: Efficiency-focused Qwen refresh that swaps standard attention for a DeltaNet-attention hybrid.

context.heading: MiniMax M2 (230B)
context.after: MiniMax's flagship returns to full attention and looks like a leaner, sparser cousin of Qwen3.

context.heading: Kimi Linear (48B-A3B)
context.after: Linear-attention hybrid that keeps a transformer backbone but replaces most full-attention layers.

context.heading: OLMo 3 (32B)
context.after: Scaled-up OLMo 3 keeps the same block design but moves to grouped-query attention.

context.heading: OLMo 3 (7B)
context.after: New transparent Allen AI model that keeps OLMo's post-norm flavor while modernizing context handling.

context.heading: DeepSeek V3.2 (671B)
context.after: DeepSeek's successor keeps the V3 template but adds sparse attention to cut long-context costs.

context.heading: Mistral Large 3 (673B)
context.after: Mistral's new flagship effectively adopts the DeepSeek architecture and retunes the expert sizes.

context.heading: Nemotron 3 Nano (30B-A3B)
context.after: NVIDIA's Nano model is the most extreme transformer-state-space hybrid in the gallery.

context.heading: Xiaomi MiMo-V2-Flash (309B)
context.after: Large MoE model that pushes sliding-window attention harder than most contemporaries.

context.heading: GLM-4.7 (355B)
context.after: Immediate GLM predecessor that stays closer to the older GLM-4.5 style before the MLA shift.

context.heading: Arcee AI Trinity Large (400B)
context.after: Arcee's flagship blends several efficiency tricks into a DeepSeek-like coarse MoE design; the AA score shown here refers to the Trinity Large Thinking checkpoint.

context.heading: GLM-5 (744B)
context.after: Huge GLM refresh that adopts both MLA and DeepSeek Sparse Attention for flagship-scale inference.

context.heading: Nemotron 3 Super (120B-A12B)
context.after: The Super variant scales up Nano and adds both latent experts and native speculative decoding support.

context.heading: Gemma 4 (31B)
context.after: Dense Gemma 4 scales the family to a 256K-context multimodal checkpoint without changing the core local-global recipe much.

context.heading: Gemma 4 (26B-A4B)
context.after: Sparse Gemma 4 variant that keeps the local:global attention backbone while swapping dense FFNs for MoE layers.

context.heading: Gemma 4 (12B)
context.after: Dense Gemma 4 12B Unified uses an encoder-free multimodal input path, while its text decoder keeps the 31B-style local-global attention recipe.

context.heading: Llama 3.2 (3B)
context.after: Small Llama baseline used to show how closely Nanbeige follows the mainstream compact decoder recipe.

context.heading: Qwen3 Coder Flash (30B-A3B)
context.after: Coding-tuned Qwen model that keeps a straightforward grouped-query MoE stack instead of the newer hybrid-attention variants.

context.heading: Kimi K2.5 (1T)
context.after: Native-multimodal Moonshot flagship that keeps the K2/DeepSeek-style MoE layout and pushes native context to 256k.

context.heading: Step 3.5 Flash (196B)
context.after: Throughput-oriented MoE model that stays competitive with much larger DeepSeek-style systems.

context.heading: Nanbeige 4.1 (3B)
context.after: Small on-device oriented model that stays close to Llama 3.2 while nudging the scaling choices.

context.heading: MiniMax-M2.5 (230B)
context.after: Popular 230B coder that opts for a classic architecture instead of the newer hybrid-attention ideas.

context.heading: Tiny Aya (3.35B)
context.after: Compact multilingual model from Cohere with a rare parallel transformer block.

context.heading: Ling 2.5 (1T)
context.after: Trillion-parameter long-context model that swaps DeltaNet for Lightning Attention.

context.heading: Qwen3.5 (397B)
context.after: Mainline Qwen refresh that brings the Next-style hybrid attention into the flagship series.

context.heading: Sarvam (30B)
context.after: Reasoning-oriented Indian-language sparse MoE that keeps GQA at the smaller size.

context.heading: Sarvam (105B)
context.after: Larger Sarvam variant keeps the sparse MoE layout but switches from GQA to MLA.

context.heading: Phi-4 (14B)
context.after: Microsoft's 14B dense Phi refresh stays close to Phi-3-medium but swaps its sliding-window attention for full-context GQA and a larger tokenizer.

context.heading: xLSTM (7B)
context.after: Recurrent 7B language model that replaces self-attention with xLSTM blocks built around matrix memory.

context.heading: GLM-4.5-Air (106B)
context.after: Compact GLM-4.5 companion that keeps the same agent-oriented sparse MoE recipe at a smaller serving footprint.

context.heading: Ouro-Thinking (2.6B)
context.after: ByteDance's dense LoopLM reuses one 48-layer MHA stack across four recurrent passes and trains an exit gate over the intermediate representations.

context.heading: INTELLECT-3 (106B)
context.after: Large-scale RL post-training of GLM-4.5-Air that keeps the compact 106B sparse MoE backbone intact.

context.heading: LongCat-Flash-Lite (68.5B-A3B)
context.after: Meituan's LongCat-Next text backbone is a lightweight MoE that shifts a large share of parameters into N-gram embeddings while keeping sparse inference around 3B active parameters.

context.heading: Mistral Small 4 (119B)
context.after: Multimodal Mistral Small refresh that jumps from the older dense 24B stack to an MLA-based sparse MoE design.

context.heading: Nemotron 3 Nano (4B)
context.after: Compact on-device hybrid that compresses Nemotron Nano 9B v2 into a mostly Mamba-2 stack with only four attention layers.

context.heading: MiniMax M2.7 (230B)
context.after: Agent-focused 230B follow-up built for self-evolution, agent harnesses, and productivity workflows.

context.heading: Gemma 4 (E2B)
context.after: Smallest Gemma 4 edge model keeps the family's hybrid attention stack and adds native audio on a phone-scale multimodal footprint. Uses per-layer embeddings, which add small layer-specific token vectors without scaling the full compute path, so its compute footprint is closer to 2.3B than a full 5.1B dense model.

context.heading: Gemma 4 (E4B)
context.after: Larger Gemma 4 edge variant keeps the same multimodal hybrid recipe but doubles width and KV heads for a stronger 128K mobile checkpoint. Uses per-layer embeddings, which add small layer-specific token vectors without scaling the full compute path, so its compute footprint is closer to 4.5B than a full 8B dense model.

context.heading: DeepSeek V4-Flash (284B)
context.after: DeepSeek's efficient V4 preview keeps the million-token architecture while reducing the MoE scale to 284B parameters and 13B active parameters.

context.heading: DeepSeek V4-Pro (1.6T)
context.after: DeepSeek's flagship V4 preview scales to 1.6T parameters and introduces compressed sparse attention plus manifold-constrained hyper-connections for million-token contexts.

context.heading: Laguna XS.2 (33B)
context.after: Poolside's open-weight agentic coding MoE uses mixed sliding-window/global attention and activates only 3B of 33B parameters per token.

context.heading: ZAYA1-8B (8.4B)
context.after: Zyphra's compact reasoning MoE pairs CCA/GQA attention updates with top-1 routed expert FFN updates to keep fewer than 1B parameters active per token.

context.heading: GLM-5.1 (744B)
context.after: Post-trained GLM refresh that keeps the GLM-5 backbone intact but targets stronger long-horizon agentic coding.

context.heading: Qwen3.6 (35B-A3B)
context.after: Compact Qwen3.6 open-weight MoE that keeps the Qwen3.5 hybrid Gated DeltaNet/Gated Attention recipe while activating only about 3B parameters.

context.heading: Kimi K2.6 (1T)
context.after: Native-multimodal K2.5 successor that keeps the same 1T sparse MoE backbone while targeting stronger long-horizon coding, design, and agent orchestration.

context.heading: Qwen3.6 (27B)
context.after: Dense Qwen3.6 model that keeps the Qwen3.5-style Gated DeltaNet/Gated Attention hybrid stack while replacing MoE blocks with dense FFNs.

context.heading: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5 (310B)
context.after: Omnimodal sparse MoE model that extends the MiMo-V2-Flash backbone with vision and audio encoders.

context.heading: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.5-Pro (1.02T)
context.after: Trillion-parameter sparse MoE model for long-horizon agentic and software-engineering tasks.

context.heading: Ling 2.6 (1T)
context.after: Ling 2.5 successor that keeps the Lightning Attention and MLA hybrid stack while adding an MTP layer for multi-token prediction.

context.heading: Tencent Hy3-preview (295B-A21B)
context.after: Tencent Hunyuan's 295B sparse MoE preview combines a dense first FFN layer, GQA with QK-Norm, and one extra MTP layer for faster generation.

context.heading: Granite 4.1 (30B)
context.after: IBM's dense 30B Granite 4.1 model keeps a straightforward long-context GQA transformer stack and improves tool calling, instruction following, and chat behavior through post-training.

context.heading: Command A+ (218B-A25B)
context.after: Cohere's open sparse MoE model scales the Command A parallel transformer block to 218B total parameters while keeping 25B active per token.

context.heading: LFM2.5 (1.2B)
context.after: Liquid AI's 1.2B LFM2.5 model keeps the 16-layer hybrid LIV convolution and GQA stack at a wider hidden size.

context.heading: LFM2.5 (350M)
context.after: Liquid AI's compact LFM2.5 model combines double-gated LIV convolution blocks with periodic GQA layers.

context.heading: LFM2.5 (8B-A1B)
context.after: Liquid AI's sparse LFM2.5 model combines LIV convolution, GQA, and MoE routing with 4 of 32 experts active per token.

context.heading: JetBrains Mellum2 Thinking (12B-A2.5B)
context.after: JetBrains' Mellum2 Thinking is a compact reasoning-tuned sparse MoE for code and agentic workflows.

context.heading: Nemotron 3 Ultra (550B-A55B)
context.after: NVIDIA's Ultra model scales the Nemotron 3 hybrid stack to 550B total parameters while keeping 55B active per token.

context.heading: North Mini Code (30B-A3B)
context.after: Cohere's compact agentic coding MoE adapts the parallel Cohere2-MoE block to a 30B total, 3B active model.

context.heading: Kimi K2.7 Code (1T)
context.after: Coding-focused K2.6 successor that keeps the same 1T sparse MoE text backbone and emphasizes long-horizon software engineering agents.

context.heading: MiniMax M3 (428B)
context.after: Native multimodal MiniMax model that adds sparse attention to an M2-style MoE backbone for 1M-token context.

context.heading: VibeThinker-3B (3B)
context.after: Qwen2.5-Coder-based dense reasoner whose gains mainly come from verifier-driven post-training rather than a new block design.

context.heading: GLM-5.2 (744B)
context.after: Long-context GLM refresh that keeps the 744B sparse MoE backbone and adds IndexShare for 1M-token DSA inference.

context.heading: Laguna XS 2.1 (33B)
context.after: Poolside's 33B Laguna refresh extends the sparse MoE architecture to 262k context while keeping about 3B parameters active per token.

context.heading: Soofi S (30B-A3B)
context.after: German-English base model that retrains the Nemotron 3 Nano architecture on 26.68T tokens with a fully documented data mixture.

context.heading: Inkling (975B)
context.after: Thinking Machines Lab's native multimodal model combines a 66-layer sparse MoE decoder with a 5:1 mix of local and global GQA.

context.heading: BTL-3 (27B)
context.after: Agent-oriented Qwen3.6-27B derivative that adds a rank-32 LoRA adapter for coding, structured tool use, and long multi-turn execution.

context.heading: Antares (1B)
context.after: Cisco Foundation AI's compact terminal agent uses a dense Granite 4.0 backbone and is post-trained with SFT and GRPO for vulnerability localization.

context.heading: Laguna S 2.1 (118B)
context.after: Poolside's 118B sparse MoE scales the Laguna XS recipe to 48 layers and 1M context while activating about 8B parameters per token.

context.heading: Motif 3 Beta (314B)
context.after: Large sparse MoE that combines Grouped Differential Latent Attention, per-expert PolyNorm, and modified mHC in a 53-layer decoder.

context.heading: Nanbeige 4.2 (3B)
context.after: Compact agentic model that runs the same 22-layer dense transformer stack twice, resulting in 44 transformer blocks (layers) without duplicating the layer weights.

context.heading: Solar Open 2 (250B)
context.after: Upstage's sparse hybrid alternates one gated GQA layer with three Kimi Delta Attention layers and reaches a 1M-token context without positional embeddings.

context.heading: Kimi K3 (2.8T)
context.after: 2.8T sparse hybrid that combines a 3:1 KDA and Gated MLA stack with Block Attention Residuals and Stable LatentMoE. It is also native multimodal, but the figure focuses on the text portion.

context.heading: Ling 3.0 Flash (124B)
context.after: Hybrid MoE that alternates five Kimi Delta Attention layers with one gated MLA layer.

context.heading: Muse Glimmer (30B)
context.after: Meta's dense 29.6B multimodal model combines a 52-layer sandwich-norm decoder with gated GQA and a separate perception encoder; the figure focuses on the text backbone.

context.heading: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning (30B-A3B)
context.after: NVIDIA's 30B hybrid model keeps 3B parameters active and extends the Nemotron 3 Nano backbone with a 1M-token context window and multi-token prediction.

context.heading: Qwen3.8 (27B)
context.after: Dense 27B native vision-language model with a 64-layer Gated DeltaNet and Gated Attention language backbone; the figure omits the vision encoder and MTP head.

context.heading: Ornith 1.5 (35B-A3B)
context.after: Uses the same sparse-hybrid decoder geometry as Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, paired with Ornith's self-improvement training recipe.

context.heading: GLM-5.3-Flash (320B)
context.after: Natively multimodal GLM refresh, previously previewed as Ox Alpha, that replaces most MLA/DSA layers with Kimi Delta Attention and adds four-stream mHC.

context.heading: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (125B-A6B)
context.after: Experimental vision-language MoE whose text backbone combines Gated DeltaNet, micro-block QSA, four-branch gated residuals, and n-gram embeddings; the figure omits the vision encoder and MTP head.

context.heading: Tencent Hy4-preview (770B-A49B)
context.after: Tencent's 770B sparse MoE combines gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention, cross-layer index reuse, and four-stream identity Hyper-Connections.

context.heading: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash (552B)
context.after: Causal encoder-decoder MoE with CSA2 cache sharing, Engram memory, and a million-token context. The figure shows the text backbone.

context.heading: Step-5 Preview (600B)
context.after: StepFun's 92-layer MoE pairs 512-token sliding-window attention with sparse GQA for a 1M-token context window; the figure shows the text decoder.

context.heading: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL (309B)
context.after: Omnimodal sparse MoE model with the MiMo-V2.5 text backbone, mixed-domain reinforcement learning, and a five-layer DFlash speculative decoder.

context.heading: Xiaomi MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL (1.02T)
context.after: Omnimodal sparse MoE model with the MiMo-V2.5-Pro text backbone, mixed-domain reinforcement learning, and a five-layer DFlash speculative decoder.

context.heading: Ember-1 (2.8T)
context.after: Fireworks' Kimi K3 derivative, post-trained for shorter reasoning traces. Architecture details follow the published Kimi K3 base model; the diagram focuses on its text backbone.

context.heading: Naive-N0.5-Flash (309B)
context.after: MiMo-V2.5-derived sparse MoE that replaces its global attention layers with GQA-based DeepSeek Sparse Attention for a native 1M-token context.

context.heading: Kolibri-1 (78B)
context.after: Aleph Alpha's German-English reasoning model uses 50 MoE blocks with a 4:1 mix of sliding-window and global GQA.

context.heading: Ling 3.1 Flash (560B)
context.after: Hybrid MoE that extends Ling 3.0 Flash to 72 layers, with seven Kimi Delta Attention layers for every gated MLA layer.

context.heading: Muse Spark Open (816B-A42B)
context.after: Meta's multimodal MoE model combines 62 latent-expert blocks with gated GQA, local-only RoPE, global NoPE, and learned residual gates; the figure focuses on the text decoder.

context.heading: Nemotron 3.5 Super VL (120B-A12B)
context.after: NVIDIA's vision-language model extends the Nemotron 3 Super backbone with C-RADIO vision encoding and shared-weight multi-token prediction. The figure shows the language backbone, with the vision encoder and MTP omitted.

context.heading: Reflection Beam (501B)
context.after: Text-only MoE decoder with three dense FFN layers followed by 49 expert layers. Each MoE layer activates 8 of 256 experts without a shared expert.

context.heading: Dory1.0 (4B)
context.after: NVIDIA's dense looped transformer applies a shared 20-block core twice between 8-block input and output stacks, using normalized GPT (nGPT) residual updates.

context.heading: Recursive Flint (40B-A2.5B)
context.after: Recursive's coding model uses two dense FFN layers followed by 47 MoE layers. The active-parameter count includes the output head.

context.heading: MiniMax M3.1-Flash (428B)
context.after: MiniMax M3 successor with sparse attention in all 60 decoder layers, quantization-aware training, and a DSpark draft head for speculative decoding.

context.heading: LFM3 (1.7B)
context.after: Liquid AI's 1.73B dense hybrid combines short convolutions with sliding-window and global GQA in a 24-layer stack.

context.heading: Mistral Large 4 (1T)
context.after: Mistral's trillion-parameter multimodal MoE combines MLA with sparse token selection and cross-layer KV sharing.

context.heading: Kimi K3.1 Pro (2.8T)
context.after: Post-trained from Kimi K3, with its 24 Gated MLA layers converted to Gated DeepSeek Sparse Attention. The figure shows the text backbone of this native multimodal model.
